chunks: Sa'd from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar and others said:
I asked him about the fitrah (semen emission), he said: When you isolate it (perform ghusl), it does not harm you when you give it (perform ghusl), before the prayer or after the prayer.

key_terms.عَزَلْتَهَا: You isolate it (referring to performing the ritual bath/ghusl)

ai.seo_question: When should one perform ghusl after seminal emission relative to prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in timing the ritual bath (*ghusl al-fitrah*) relative to the obligatory prayer, indicating that performing it before or after does not invalidate the prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that *ghusl* is a condition for the validity of prayer but not necessarily a prerequisite for its initial performance if one is in a state of major impurity, provided it is completed before the prayer time ends. The narration underscores the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted to believers in managing ritual purity amidst daily obligations.
